messages:
aisha-oncall: :rotating_light: Pager triggered - multiple 503s across services in us-west-2a. ELB unhealthy counts spiking, console shows instance drain. Can someone pick this up?

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-9843 - us-west-2a elevated 5xxs. Paging aisha-oncall, tom-infra. PagerDuty: triggered.

tom-infra: I see the spike on the ELB health_fail metric for app-prod-elb-usw2a, started ~2798743180. Totals: 62 failed checks in 3m.

marta-sre: checking instance status - a handful of ec2 instances reporting IMDS request errors in cloudwatch agent logs. Could be token fetch failures (IMDSv2).

raj-platform: any recent AMI changes or startup script edits? Not seeing deploys in that AZ in the last hour.

elain-cs: multiple customer reports about API timeouts (some 10-20% of requests). Sending affected customer IDs to CS channel.

aisha-oncall: I'm jumping in. Tom, run a quick IMDS test on a sample instance in the AZ:
```
# from bastion
curl -s -I --connect-timeout 2 http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token -X PUT -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 21600" -v
```

tom-infra: ran it, getting 500/connection reset intermittently. Also seeing a lot of 429 from metadata service in logs: "TooManyRequestsException".

marta-sre: that would break any agent/sidecar that refreshes tokens frequently -> could cause healthcheck scripts to fail if they depend on metadata (IAM creds for pulling config). ELB sees unhealthy targets and starts draining.

aisha-oncall: Good find. Plan: 1) mitigate customer impact by routing traffic away from us-west-2a (Route53 weight shift + ELB cross-zone balancing), 2) reduce token churn on instances (increase IMDS token TTL in app config where possible), 3) wfh with AWS support for regional IMDS throttling. I'll start the DNS weight shift.

raj-platform: I'll create a temporary traffic policy: Route53 weighted record set for api.prod.example.com - reduce us-west-2a weight to 5% from 50%, shift remainder to us-west-2b/c. Proceeding now.

incident-bot: Route53 change submitted: change-id Z1234abcd. Expected propagation ~30s-2m.

elaine-cs: passing update to affected customers: "We're mitigating an availability issue in one AWS AZ; routing traffic to healthy AZs now. We'll update when full service restored."

tom-infra: after weight shift latency on requests dropped per dashboards. ELB unhealthy count for us-west-2a decreased but still some flaps as instances keep failing healthchecks.

marta-sre: quick remediation we can do for impacted instances: restart metadata-dependent agents only (cloudwatch-agent, sidecar auth daemon) to reduce token churn and backoff quickly. Doing a rolling restart on suspect instances (non-disruptive).

aisha-oncall: Do it in small batches (2 at a time) and monitor ELB target health. Use this command to restart the sidecar:
```
sudo systemctl restart auth-sidecar || sudo systemctl restart cwagent
```

raj-platform: also toggling ELB healthcheck grace period to 60s temporarily to avoid flapping while services recover. Changing target group health settings now.

incident-bot: TargetGroup update applied: health check interval 30s -> 10s? (edited) Actually we lowered the unhealthy threshold to avoid premature drain — confirm.

tom-infra: FYI, AWS status page for ec2 in us-west-2 shows "Investigating - Elevated error rates for instance metadata service in a subset of capacity" (link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/XYZ). Raising support case.

marta-sre: running a quick script to detect instances with high metadata error rates:
```
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --metric-name MetadataErrors --namespace EC2/IMDS --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value=i-... --start-time ... --end-time ... --statistics Sum
```

aisha-oncall: rolling restart batch 1 complete, ELB target healthy count +3. Continuing batches.

pagerduty: Acknowledged by aisha-oncall. Escalation level: SEV2.

elaine-cs: customers updated: major customers seeing improvement after traffic shift, CS will keep monitoring.

raj-platform: AWS support responded: they confirmed localized IMDS rate limiting from control plane issue, working on mitigation; estimated mitigation 1-2 hours. They recommended: reduce token request rate, increase TTL, and avoid parallel restarts that cause token storms.

marta-sre: we'll patch app config to increase token TTL from 30m -> 12h on services that can accept it (feature flags already exist). Rolling out to non-critical clusters first.

aisha-oncall: next steps: 1) keep Route53 weight at reduced level until AWS confirms full recovery, 2) finish token-TTL config rollout, 3) monitor ELB target counts, 4) prepare post-incident summary.

tom-infra: checkpoint - total customer error rate in last 15m peaked at 18%, now down to 3% after mitigations. Charts: https://dashboards.redwood.net/d/abcd/usw2a-elb-health

incident-bot: Update: AWS support status changed to "Service degradation resolved for some customers", monitoring continues.

elaine-cs: CS thread reports no new customer escalations in last 20m. Keeping on-call notification until full recovery.

aisha-oncall: handing off to daytime oncall marta-sre. I'll write runbook notes in the incident doc and drop a summary. Marta, please continue monitoring and coordinate with AWS for closure.

marta-sre: ack, taking over. I'll keep the weight shift in place for now and keep token TTL rollout moving.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by marta-sre. Pager cleared for aisha-oncall.

final note by aisha-oncall: summary for postmortem - root cause: regional IMDS rate limiting in us-west-2a causing token fetch failures -> sidecar/auth failures -> ELB health checks failing -> increased 503s. Mitigations: Route53 weight shift, restart/reduce token churn, increase TTL, adjust healthcheck thresholds. Follow-up: evaluate retry/backoff in sidecar token logic, add IMDS error rate alerting, automate graceful weight shift playbook.
